[1/2] Add a first-class AegeanWorks Editor page that embeds the Palette image editor in a same-origin iframe. [2/2] Vendor the 16-file Palette runtime with a content-hash manifest, wire nav, sitemap and service-worker precache, and add source-sync plus site-integrity tests.

impact_assessment.why: The user asked for a Photoshop-style static image editor that can be integrated into the AegeanWorks website; Palette lives in its own AIKit project, so the site needs a reproducible, verifiable copy and a real page.
impact_assessment.benefits: A local-first editor reachable from every page's navigation, no uploads, no third-party runtime, a self-contained published build, and a content-hash gate that catches a stale copy.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the site iframe, CSP and navigation are public surfaces; dependency: the vendored copy can drift from the Palette source; concurrency: the single-threaded editor is unaffected, but a service-worker update can arrive between page loads, so the precache stays explicit and versioned; state: service-worker caching can serve mixed versions and iframe keyboard focus needs a clear hand-off.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Copy only the declared runtime, record per-file SHA-256 plus a combined source hash, verify the copy with sync_editor --check, add Python tests for manifest integrity, navigation, sitemap and precache, and verify the embedded app in a real headless browser.

Site tests 89/89 and a headless iframe boot check pass. checklists: passed (test, hygiene, guidelines, secrets; G-001 declines a UI review, so automated browser/site proof is the UI evidence).
